messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change only the person's one-piece garment to match the reference images (front and back views). Preserve the garment's design, color, pattern, and details from the references. Leave the rest of the outfit and everything else in the video unchanged.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: Please change only the person's one-piece garment to match the reference images. Leave the rest of the outfit and everything else in the video unchanged.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The character stands still, then raises both arms overhead and swings them in a rhythmic dance motion before returning to a standing pose.","camera":"Static medium-full shot from behind the character at a slightly low angle.","clothing":"White long-sleeved shirt, orange Y-back suspenders, and tan pants with a dark grid pattern.","hair_color":"Bright blue.","hairstyle":"Hair is pulled up into a high top-knot bun with a short tail hanging down the back of the neck.","identity":"A 3D-rendered male video game character with a slim build, seen from behind.","scene":"An outdoor paved road or parking area under a blue sky, with a street lamp, a metal guardrail, and trees with yellow and green leaves."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The character's original dark one-piece outfit was replaced with a light/white long-sleeved shirt, orange Y-back suspenders, and tan pants with a dark grid pattern. The character's blue hair, pose, dance motion, camera angle, outdoor road scene, and lighting remain essentially the same.
arguments.requested_change: Change only the person's one-piece garment to match the reference images, preserving the reference garment's design, color, pattern, and details while leaving the rest of the outfit and everything else unchanged.
uncertain: Whether the shirt's fine pattern and button details exactly match the reference front view.
unexpected_changes: The replaced garment's colors differ from the references: the pants appear tan/light rather than dark, and the suspenders appear orange rather than brown.
